title: Sameday AI vs Avoca
seo_title: Sameday AI vs Avoca: Pricing & Business Fit
description: Sameday AI vs Avoca: compare phone products, coaching, human backup and pricing. See where Off The Clock’s operator and QuoteDone differ.
intro: Both offer more than a voice answering calls. The useful distinction is what they add around the conversation—and whether job pricing still lands on you.
verdict: Choose Off The Clock when your priority is answering, quoting and booking in one customer interaction. QuoteDone brings your prices and job details together; the operator handles the questions, transfers and follow-up around them.

sections: Call analysis and quote completion are different purchases

Both vendors describe coaching. Avoca’s Coach emphasizes assessing calls and reporting outcomes. Sameday presents coaching beside its phones and scheduling products. [[avoca-coach]] [[sameday-product]]

That analysis can describe how a conversation went. It does not, by itself, calculate a project from the owner’s rates. For the owner still preparing prices after well-handled calls, a better call score is not the same deliverable as an answered price question.
An outside CSR and your own team are not interchangeable

Avoca documents trained CSRs in North America as part of its Human in the Loop program. Its availability and price are program terms, not something this page assumes is included in every subscription. [[avoca-human]]

Off The Clock’s human route is to your business team. That keeps business-specific judgment with the people responsible for it, while QuoteDone handles supported routine prices. External receptionist staffing is not included in the Off The Clock offer.
Choose the outcome that removes the next task

A customer can provide a service, measurements and selected extras, then still leave the owner with a quote to build. QuoteDone is the part of Off The Clock designed to close that gap: your approved rates applied to the complete supported request.

The operator still answers business questions, books, transfers and follows up. The website widget provides a second entry point. Unknown measurements remain in a review request rather than turning into a made-up price; the benefit is less repeat intake, not less control.
The subscription and the modules behind it

Sameday publishes Launch at $449 with 500 minutes and Scale at $789 with 1,000. The reviewed Avoca product pages do not establish a comparable subscription amount. The selected Avoca modules and human coverage determine its proposal. [[sameday-pricing]] [[avoca-product]]

Off The Clock’s QuoteDone offer is $279 for 1,200 minutes, the operator and website quote widget. Extra usage is $0.35 per minute, with no setup fee. The scope of that subscription is the customer inquiry and its price—not outsourced staffing or a replacement coaching suite.
decision: Choose Off The Clock when the owner’s unfinished task is the job price. You are buying an operator with QuoteDone, so the next useful step can happen during the inquiry rather than waiting for another conversation with you.
card_description: Sameday publishes minute packages; Avoca documents coaching and a trained-human program. Compare those purchases with owner-priced job quoting.
